title: Industrial communication basics
summary: Ethernet, IP addresses, subnets and Modbus TCP: how a PLC reads a value from a device over the network.
objectives: Explain IP address and subnet mask

sections.heading: Networks in the plant
sections.body: Modern devices exchange data over Ethernet. Each device has an **IP address** and a **subnet mask**; devices in the same subnet talk directly, others need a **gateway**. Protocols such as Modbus TCP, PROFINET or EtherNet/IP define the data exchange.

sections.heading: A Modbus TCP read
sections.body: The PLC is the client, the transmitter the server.
sections.diagram:
PLC 192.168.0.10 --request FC03 addr 0 qty 3--> transmitter 192.168.0.20
  PLC <-------------- response: 3 registers ------- transmitter
  (timeout if no answer, exception if the request is invalid)

sections.heading: Guarding the value
sections.body: Never use a value from a lost connection.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Confusing the documented register 40001 with protocol address 1. Modbus addresses on the wire start at 0, so 40001 is address 0.

question.question: PLC 192.168.0.10/24. Which device is reachable without a gateway?
question.explanation: Only 192.168.0.x is in the same /24 subnet.

sections.heading: Practice: Modbus level
sections.body: Fill a tank using a level transmitter on Modbus TCP and stop on communication loss.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Devices communicate when addresses, subnets and protocol settings match; values from failed connections must not drive the process.

**Troubleshooting note:** Read the connection status first: timeout, connection refused, no route and exception each point to a different cause.
